audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart said 'Skill' on 6 of 7 rows while win[0..6] and the packet levelChart both say Cassiopeia, and every why/whys sentence describes Cassiopeia winning.
audit.why: 52.44% over 1888 games with the prose and the content layer already Cassiopeia-favoured; the full-layer side was the odd layer out.
audit.corrected: phases[0..4].side and phases[6].side set to Cassiopeia, matching win[N] which already read Cassiopeia. Difficulty stays EVEN-leaning-favoured at 5.5/10.

audit.why: Spikes are real: Sylas level 3 combo, Hijack at 6 (R 80/55/30), Cassiopeia's first DoT item, full build.
audit.corrected: Left spikes[0..3] intact; only wants.foe[2] mis-sourced his sustain.

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction was never stated: Miasma (W) grounds, and both Abscond and its Abduct recast are movement abilities. Sustain was attributed to Petricite Burst (a passive attack-empower) instead of Kingslayer (W).
audit.why: Riot text: Abscond dashes, recast pulls Sylas to an enemy hit; Kingslayer 'lunges at an enemy... healing himself against enemy champions'. Petricite Burst gives bonus magic damage and attack speed, no healing.
audit.corrected: Stated grounding of Abscond/Abduct with the E cooldown (13/12/11/10/9), stated Kingslayer as the heal (12/10.5/9/7.5/6) and flagged Grievous Wounds, and noted Hijack turning Petrifying Gaze back on you.

audit.why: It is the field that must carry real numbers.
audit.corrected: E 13s at rank 1 / 9s at rank 5, W heal every 12s early, Miasma 24s at rank 1.

audit.whatIsWrong: Anti-heal against Kingslayer was only in the report, and wants.foe[2] named the wrong ability.
Two bullets were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad pastes under unrelated titles, and two more were generic template lines.
audit.why: lintFindings COPY_PASTE_BLEED on dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d.
audit.corrected: Bodies rewritten to match their titles using Petrifying Gaze facing rules, the Abduct recast, and Q ranges (850 vs 775).

edits.before: - Sylas Abscond / Abduct: matchup-defining — Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget R Petrifying Gaze for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Abscond / Abduct is his only gap-closer: 13s at rank 1, 9s at rank 5. Step up on that window. - Kingslayer heals him off you every 12s early. - Miasma is 24s at rank 1, so hold it for his E, not for the wave.

edits.before: Sylas wins by landing Abscond / Abduct, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Sylas wins by Abducting you into Chain Lash, healing the trade back with Kingslayer, and turning your own Petrifying Gaze on you with Hijack.

edits.before: Carry by DPS — no mid matches your damage-per-second from two items; your job is staying alive long enough to prove it.
edits.after: Carry by grounding: Miasma turns off Abscond, Abduct and his Hijacked mobility, so he cannot reach you while fangs tick him down.

edits.before: Ahead, suffocate: poison every last-hit, zone Sylas off the wave with fang threat, and call your jungler — your W makes every gank a guaranteed kill.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the reset: Kingslayer is how he stays in lane, so poke him off the wave and ground his E the moment your jungler steps into the river.

edits.before: If Sylas gets a kill, the lane gets honest — give Abscond / Abduct extra room and farm it back. Two kills: stop dueling your tilt — farm with Q-E clears and stay relevant through grounded peel.
edits.after: If Sylas gets a kill, respect the 400-range Abscond and give it room — farm it back with Q-E clears. Two kills: stop dueling, and hold Miasma purely for his engage so you still peel through grounding.

edits.before: Q the last-hit window, E-E-E while the poison ticks, and walk back as it fades — three fangs and out, repeat until Sylas is executable.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze only stuns enemies facing you — turn into his Abduct pull instead of running, and a 120s ultimate lands as a stun rather than a slow.

edits.before: Sylas spends Abscond / Abduct early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Q reaches 850 to his 775 Chain Lash — poke his farm approach and walk out of the delayed blast.

edits.before: That is Sylas’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Spend it on wave and his E arrives ungrounded for the next 24 seconds.

edits.before: Spamming unpoisoned fangs at full mana cost, or holding W so long the dash you were saving it for already happened.
edits.after: His E recast pulls him to whoever it hits — chasing past your own miasma hands him a free re-engage with Kingslayer healing.

edits.before: No permanent owner here — the level chart shows where momentum tilts and tilts back.
edits.after: You own every row: poison out-trades Chain Lash early and Miasma denies Abscond after.

edits.before: Track Sylas’s Abscond / Abduct: Dash into chain-stun — punish him hard while it is down. Forward steps wait for its downtime.
edits.after: Miasma grounds Abscond and Abduct — drop it under his feet and both the dash and the recast pull fail. Punish the 13s window it is down.

edits.before: Use Petricite Burst sustain to win extended trades and out-heal your poison DoT
edits.after: Use Kingslayer healing off you every 12s to out-sustain your poison damage

edits.before: Once you land your first DoT item your poison damage plus Twin Fang execute range simply outpaces his sustained self-heal from Petricite Burst.
edits.after: Once you land your first DoT item, poison plus Twin Fang outpaces his Kingslayer healing — add Grievous Wounds here and his extended trades stop working.

notes: Sylas is male (he/him) — no pronoun defects found. Petricite Burst is an attack-empower passive with attack speed, not a heal; the heal is Kingslayer (W), which is what the packet suspectName on wants.foe[2] was actually pointing at. Level chart: full-layer sides were 'Skill' while win[N] already read Cassiopeia, so only the side rows needed moving — win[N] required no paired edit because it was already correct, and the whys already describe Cassiopeia winning. Left phases[N].rating alone (5-6/10 is consistent with a 52.44% even-ish lane). Whether Hijack can copy Petrifying Gaze's facing-dependent stun exactly as Cassiopeia casts it is not in the kit text; I stated only that he can turn your ultimate on you, which Hijack's own text supports.
